narrativeSummary: June 8 was a session that opened in crisis and closed in cautious optimism — the fourth time this pattern has played out since the Iran war began. Overnight, the Israeli Air Force struck military targets in western and central Iran, and Iran fired missiles at Israel for the first time since the original ceasefire agreement, threatening to unravel the fragile truce. Asian markets responded harshly: South Korea's Kospi fell 8%, Japan's Nikkei dropped 3.85%, SoftBank fell 7.5%. US futures opened lower. Then came the reversal. Trump posted on Truth Social that Israel and Iran 'are looking to do an immediate CEASEFIRE!' and that 'final negotiations' were proceeding with things set to 'move quickly.' WTI crude, which had spiked above $93-94 intraday, pulled back to close around $91.30 — still elevated but off the day's highs. Equity markets seized on the ceasefire signal and the session flipped. The dominant story became the reversal trade in semiconductors. SOXX rose nearly 7% — its best single day in over a year — as the names most brutally sold on Friday (Intel +12%, Micron +14%, Marvell +14%) snapped back sharply. CNBC noted the rebound was a textbook mean-reversion: the worst decile from Friday was up over 2.5% on Monday, with returns declining steadily across the performance spectrum. Citi's analysis was constructive: SOXX is still up 91% in 2026 despite Friday's rout, with semiconductor earnings per share expected to grow 12% in 2027. The AI infrastructure demand story received two fresh confirmations: Corning announced an Amazon fiber optic deal worth billions, popping 9%; Cerebras surged 17% on bullish initiations from nine Wall Street firms including Barclays, Citi, Morgan Stanley, Needham, and Wedbush. Apple +2% as WWDC kicked off with AI strategy updates to Siri and iOS. Marvell +14% (beyond intraday gains) on S&P 500 inclusion announcement for June 22. Critically, Nvidia was the session's notable underperformer at -0.39% — its modest gain compared to semis rebounding 12-14% suggests the market is differentiating within AI hardware. The 10Y yield edged higher to 4.568% from Friday's 4.55% official, and the 30Y to 5.039% from 5.01% — rates markets are not celebrating the ceasefire signal yet, as the NFP print remains the dominant macro data point ahead of Warsh's June 17 FOMC debut.
macroStressSubtext: Israel-Iran strikes overnight reversed by Trump ceasefire post; semi rebound -12pt MSI from 82. But NFP 172K hike risk and 10Y 4.57% keep regime firmly High ahead of Warsh June 17.
rateCurveRead: Yields rose modestly on June 8 despite the Trump ceasefire signal — the bond market is not yet pricing Iran resolution as a done deal. The 10Y edged to 4.568% (confirmed CNBC live quote) from the H.15 June 5 official of 4.55%, and the 30Y to 5.039% from 5.01%. The 2Y moved slightly higher to approximately 4.19%, reflecting the continued pricing of the NFP 172K print and the 72.7% year-end hike probability. The curve's lack of reaction to the Iran ceasefire signal is telling: the bond market learned from prior false dawns (three separate de-escalation trades since April that partially reversed) and is waiting for a formally signed agreement before adjusting the long-end inflation premium. Warsh June 17 remains the structural anchor — all eyes on May CPI (June 11) as the final inflation data point before his inaugural FOMC. risks.title: June CPI May 11 — the last inflation data before Warsh June 17. If >3.7%, hike near-certain.
risks.desc: May CPI will be released June 11 — three trading days before Warsh's June 17 FOMC debut. This single data point will be the most consequential in the cycle. If May CPI prints above 3.7%, the rate hike at June 17 becomes near-certain. If it prints below 3.5% (energy deflation from WTI $88-91 range), Warsh can hold with confidence. The World Cup distortion in NFP (Leisure & Hospitality +70K) does not affect CPI — so the CPI print is a clean read on the inflation trajectory.

risks.title: Israel-Iran ceasefire fragility — fourth near-collapse in two months
risks.desc: This was the fourth episode of Israel-Iran strikes threatening to unravel the ceasefire. Each time Trump has intervened diplomatically via social media to stabilise the situation. But the pattern has a limit: at some point, the military escalation may exceed Trump's ability to resolve it via a Truth Social post. Iran firing missiles at Israel for the first time since the ceasefire is qualitatively different from prior Qeshm-style targeted strikes. The fragility is structural — until a formal signed agreement with verified Hormuz reopening, every night holds the same risk.

risks.title: Warsh June 17 inaugural FOMC — 72.7% hike probability with 172K NFP and 3.8% CPI
risks.desc: fedTransitionRisk at 88. Warsh faces: NFP 172K (2x consensus, World Cup caveat), CPI 3.8%, core PCE 3.2%, 10Y near 4.57%, and an Iran oil supply shock that Barclays says takes 60-90 days to resolve even with a deal. His public record favours tighter policy. The market has priced a 72.7% hike by year-end — but if Warsh signals a June 17 hike explicitly, the market reaction would be severe (Nasdaq -8-12%). The June 11 CPI print is the last chance to shift the narrative before the meeting.

In a tighter macro environment (NFP shock, rate hike risk), a capital-intensive growth company without near-term S&P inclusion loses a major structural demand source. The Cerebras precedent (+68% first day) is the bull case; the Quantinuum -8% below IPO price is the bear case.

Citi's constructive view — SOXX up 91% in 2026, semi EPS +12% in 2027, maintain AVGO/TXN/AMAT — is well-grounded. If June CPI (June 11) prints below 3.5% on energy deflation, the rate hike fear reverses and semis benefit from both lower discount rates and intact AI demand. The risk: if June CPI is hot (>3.7%), Warsh hikes June 17 and semis reprice lower from the current partially-recovered level.
strategies.trigger: June CPI <3.6% AND Warsh June 17 holds rates

strategies.title: Long Corning — Amazon + Nvidia fiber deals confirm AI optical networking as structural multi-year spend
strategies.body: Corning now has multi-billion fiber deals with both Amazon (AI data centres) and Nvidia (announced May 6, $500M). The optical networking bottleneck is the next AI infrastructure constraint after compute (NVDA) and memory (MU). GLW at 22x forward earnings with confirmed hyperscaler demand is the cheapest AI infrastructure name on a risk-adjusted basis. 1,000 North Carolina jobs from the Amazon deal confirms the US manufacturing dimension. This is not a trade — it's a multi-year AI picks-and-shovels position.
strategies.trigger: Amazon and Nvidia deals begin deliveries AND additional hyperscaler deal announced

strategies.title: June CPI binary hedge — long TLT puts (hot CPI) AND long TLT calls (cool CPI)
strategies.body: May CPI (June 11) is the most consequential single data point in the cycle. The two-tail distribution: (1) Hot CPI >3.7% → Warsh hikes June 17 → 10Y to 4.8%+ → TLT falls sharply; (2) Cool CPI <3.4% on energy deflation → Warsh holds comfortably → 10Y falls to 4.2-4.3% → TLT rallies 5-7%. The World Cup hiring distortion in NFP makes the CPI more important as a clean inflation read. A June CPI straddle using TLT options expiring June 20 captures both tails at ~18 VIX cost.
strategies.trigger: June CPI release June 11 — position before, harvest after

strategies.title: SpaceX IPO Friday — approach with discipline given S&P exclusion and Eisman concerns
strategies.body: SpaceX IPO proceeds Friday at $1.77T. The Cerebras precedent (20x oversubscribed, +68% first day) and institutional demand are the bull case. The bear case: capital intensity, asteroid mining speculation, S&P 500 exclusion for a year (no passive buying), Steve Eisman's skepticism, and a hawkish macro backdrop (NFP 172K, rate hike 72.7%). Strategy: small IPO allocation if available; if stock opens >25% above IPO price, wait for a first-week pullback below 15% premium. The lack of S&P inclusion removes the automatic institutional buying that made Marvell's 14% Monday gain possible.
strategies.trigger: SpaceX IPO priced at or above $1.77T AND first-day close within 20% of IPO price
